source_text: In modern contexts, extremist groups have invoked Islamic justifications for forced circumcisions on non-Muslims during conflicts, as seen in 2001 when militants in Ambon, Indonesia, subjected Christian men, women, and children to the procedure amid sectarian violence, citing religious purification despite mainstream scholarly consensus against compulsion in faith matters.
